fact: The Controller of Budget's review of the 12 months to 30 June 2026, as reported by the Daily Nation, says county governments process payroll in the national Human Resource Information System (HRIS-Ke), to which an April 2024 directive required them to migrate by June 2025, while at least Sh8.3 billion in salaries was still paid by manual payroll outside it; Narok and Trans Nzoia reported no manual payments, and 'connectivity challenges' were among the reasons counties cited for manual payroll. The report does not say where the staff entering payroll sit or how the offices are connected.

The National Treasury's draft National Payment System Policy of August 2026 says the Central Bank of Kenya migrated government payments to its real-time gross settlement system and rolled out internet banking for ministries, departments and agencies and for county governments; it gives no date, no count of counties and nothing on how county offices are connected, so the date here is the document's published date.
system: County governments' use of Central Bank of Kenya internet banking

fact: The National Treasury's IFMIS website describes the Integrated Financial Management Information System as an automated platform for planning, budgeting, procurement, expenditure management and reporting within both the national and the county governments, with real-time monitoring; it gives no date, no count of counties and nothing on how county offices are connected, so the date here is the day the page was retrieved, which the record uses as its published date.

We Are Tech Africa reports that the National Treasury's Cabinet Secretary announced on 25 August 2026, after meeting the Council of Governors, that all 47 county governments must finish integrating the national electronic procurement platform (e-GP) with IFMIS by 30 September 2026; e-GP was due to extend to all national and local administrations from 1 July 2025, the Council of Governors resisted the pace, and more than 900 public entities of all kinds had migrated by February 2026, with no count of counties given and nothing on how county offices are connected.
system: County governments' use of e-GP and IFMIS

system: County governments' use of the Human Resource Information System
